dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: What an interesting woven scroll... Oh, hello there. You're new around here, aren't you? What can I help you with?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me about the era you lived in?

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: Hehe, compared to the ages the others speak of, mine was rather uneventful.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: Remuria and the Lochknight existed only in plays, and the intricate machines of later centuries had yet to appear for another thousand years.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: So if you were hoping I could share some exciting story from my era, I fear it may sound rather dull.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: As for me, Cirsteen de Pincerais, I was merely the daughter of a rather ordinary viscount. Even in my own time, our house could hardly stand beside great families like the de Petrichors or the Randolphs.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: Ah, these exhibits? I've heard they were woven by the people of ancient Natlan. I can't say I fully understand them, but they're lovely to look at.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: It does make one curious, though... Why did they develop a tradition like this? In our dear Fontaine, picture books actually appeared later than written text...

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: Miss Vindia — the "Madam Snow-Winged Goose" — had never even heard of picture books. In her era, pigments seemed to be used only for military purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Cirsteen
dialogues.text: Natlan... it truly is a fascinating place.
